current_answer: As of 31 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular models. AI Stupid Level’s API-side tracker reports no confirmed alarm among 25 models, but two early watches: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on coding and tool use, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite on reasoning; these are below-baseline warnings, not confirmed detector fires. Google’s API documentation now says gemini-3.5-flash requests are automatically routed to gemini-3.6-flash, establishing a serving/product identity change that can explain why a model name is not a fixed version, but not showing quality declined. The 27 October ABIS behavior-change finding for Gemini 3.5 Flash remains a behavior signal, not a capability verdict; Flash Lite is a separate label. LiveNerf’s completed Opus 5.5 window still reports no change on one pinned Claude Code subscription path, while its later window remains in progress. NerfBench’s latest displayed session remains 16 October and its score combines correctness, output tokens, and cost. A newly inspected user account describes ChatGPT text-instruction and image-generation friction with renewal intent; it supplies neither a matched replay nor prevalence. For an API user whose old Gemini string behaves differently, capture the requested model name and available response metadata, then compare a safe recurring task using the current documented route before attributing the change to capability.

catalogue_card.question: Why did the Gemini 3.5 Flash result change?
catalogue_card.text: Google says the old API model name now routes to Gemini 3.6 Flash. That verifies a serving-path change, not a quality drop; two separate tracker watches remain unconfirmed.

summary: Broad capability decline across popular AI models is not established as of 31 October 2026.

AI Stupid Level’s API-side tracker snapshot at 07:47 UTC reports no confirmed alarm among 25 models, but two early watches: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on coding and tool use, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite on reasoning. Both are unconfirmed; 66 of 75 suite detectors are armed and three models are calibrating.

Google’s Gemini API documentation, last updated 30 October, says requests using gemini-3.5-flash are automatically routed to gemini-3.6-flash; the old name is no longer selectable in AI Studio. This confirms a product/serving change, not a quality decline or its cause.
The 27 October ABIS Gemini 3.5 Flash behavior-change signal remains a behavior signal, not a capability verdict. Its Flash label is distinct from the tracker’s Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite watch.
LiveNerf’s latest completed Claude Opus 5.5 window remains “no change” on one pinned Claude Code subscription path; the subsequent window was still in progress in its 29 October status.
BridgeBench NerfBench still shows 16 October as its latest session. Its “power” score combines correctness, output tokens, and cost, so it is not a pure quality measure.
One new community post links instruction-following and image-generation friction to a self-reported intention not to renew ChatGPT Pro; the account is not a matched test or a representative sample.
For an API behavior change, capture the requested model name and response metadata; compare a safe repeated task on the currently documented route before attributing the outcome to model capability.
uncertainty: AI Stupid Level’s tasks and serving conditions are operator-controlled; its two early watches are not confirmed alerts.
Google’s model page does not state when the automatic route began or whether it matches the date of ABIS’s signal.
LiveNerf is a narrow task panel, and its current completed result ends 23 October; no equivalent representative consumer test was found.
BridgeBench’s latest visible tests are from 16 October, and its composite includes tokens and cost as well as correctness.
Community reports lack matched artifacts and a representative denominator.
First-party analytics are unavailable; reach, return use, task outcomes, renewal, switching, and funding remain unknown.
freshness_note: Checked 31 October 2026 at 12:08 UTC. Google documents that gemini-3.5-flash API requests are automatically routed to gemini-3.6-flash, but the page gives no effective date. The current tracker has two unconfirmed watches and no confirmed alarm; its private API task set is not a consumer-app test.
